non_rust_exception_baseline._comment: FROZEN review-visible baseline of TODAY's accepted temporary_legacy_bridge non-Rust automation exceptions (the exceptions[] allowlist). The file-extension scan permits a non-Rust file iff it has an exceptions[] entry (any-allowlisted-ok); this dimension additionally freezes that EXCEPTION SET shrink-only so a NEW .py/.sh bridge cannot be admitted by silently adding an allowlist row. A current exception NOT in this baseline is born-blocking (rust_first_automation_unbaselined_non_rust_exception) -- convert it to owned Rust (e.g. a contract-slice entry on //ci/facade/contract-slice-conformance) rather than shell/Python; a removed bridge must shrink this baseline in the SAME PR (rust_first_automation_non_rust_exception_baseline_stale). Folded INTO this policy (zero new tracked accounting rows); NOT producer-regenerated -- reviewed, hand-shrunk; anti-laundering is REVIEW-VISIBLE: growing the bridge set now requires an explicit reviewed baseline edit, not a routine-looking allowlist append.

_provenance.policy: shrink-only; growth requires a review-visible baseline edit, retirement must shrink in the same PR

product_contract.ci_hygiene: The scanner is read-only, creates no temporary files, and detects stale exceptions so policy debt cleans up after retired files.
product_contract.cloud_native: Exceptions must point toward Rust cloud-ci, Kubernetes, GitOps, controller, or admission-policy replacements; new infrastructure packages must be app/gate/controller/API-shaped, not CLI-shaped.
product_contract.execution: Enforced by the cargo merge path (cargo test --workspace, ADR-0716) and locally via buck2; no standalone runner contract.
product_contract.portability: Policy is data-driven so another repository can adopt the same gate by changing scan roots and exceptions.

purpose: Rust-first automation hygiene ratchet. Non-Rust scripts are blocked unless explicitly exceptioned as shrinkable debt with a Rust/cloud-native replacement path; cloud/infra/tooling CLI-first package births are blocked outright; workflow inline shell is ratcheted against a frozen keyed baseline with a reviewed replacement window for deliberate CI redesigns.

cli_package_authority._comment: Cloud-native infrastructure automation must not be born as a new CLI-first package. This dimension scans infrastructure/cloud/tooling Cargo manifests for package names with retired CLI suffixes.

interpreter_command_authority._comment: G006 inventory-first guard: Rust automation/gate source must not re-authorize retired Python/Node/MJS authority by spawning interpreter commands directly. The dead cloud/cloud-ci root is retained to avoid scan-scope-narrowing findings; retire it in a change whose subject is the shrink.

workflow_forbidden_uses._comment: Forbid third-party / marketplace buck2 setup actions. The allowed bridge is repo-owned infra/ci/install-buck2.sh, which downloads the official facebook/buck2 release asset and verifies the pinned SHA-256 before execution.

workflow_inline_shell._comment: pipeline-glue(a): parses the declared workflow roots with a real YAML parser, emits one schema-v2 keyed observation per (file, job, required unique run-step name) with exact effective-command shell_lines, and ratchets it against the embedded workflow_inline_shell_baseline. New keys or line-count growth are born-blocking EXCEPT via a reviewed replacement_window (+1 schema_version + substantive reason + a new Accepted ADR absent from the protected merge-base); retired keys or line-count shrink must shrink the baseline in the same PR. Missing or duplicate names fail closed.

workflow_inline_shell_baseline._comment: FROZEN exact named-step baseline of accepted workflow inline shell. Each entry is {key, shell_lines}, keyed as <workflow-relpath>::<job-id>::<required unique run-step name>. ADR-0716 replaced the whole baseline in one reviewed window: the CI merge path moved from buck2 to cargo, all job/step names became self-explanatory and debranded, and the cache-integrity canary plus the docs-graph-drift adapter were retired.

_provenance.authority: pipeline-glue(a): rust-first ratchet workflow-inline-shell; door:one-way except a reviewed replacement_window (+1 schema_version + reason + a new Accepted ADR absent from origin/dev) admits a deliberate CI redesign

replacement_window.reason: ADR-0718-D1 moves the advisory `Clippy, warnings denied` step out of the blocking `lint` job into its own parallel `clippy` job. The baseline is keyed <file>::<job>::<step>, so a job move is a REMOVE plus an ADD rather than a shrink, and the shrink-only ceiling correctly refuses it without this window. No new inline shell is introduced and no step is waived: the same single-line `run:` step keeps the same command and the same shell_lines, and the key count is unchanged at 24. Second authorized change in the same window: the `Materialize generated faces` step grows from 1 shell line to 4. It backgrounds `cargo build --workspace --tests` so the workspace COMPILES WHILE buck2 materializes. Measured, the two steps are 681s and 192s and run strictly in series today; they are independent because no build.rs reads materializer output and the gate crates read the faces at RUNTIME via root.join(), not include_str!. This is a deliberate and acknowledged INCREASE in workflow shell against a policy whose direction is shrink: three lines of orchestration buy back roughly 190 seconds of wall clock, GitHub Actions has no native intra-job parallelism to express it declaratively, and the step still owns no branching or git topology. It is recorded here rather than hidden so the burn-down target stays honest.
